svg.text: Local-first Zero Trust edge decisioning · Secure cloud artifact synchronisation · Runtime KB/policy reload · Calibrated trust control
☁ CLOUD / CONTROL PLANE — offline preparation · calibration · secure packaging · versioned artifact distribution
• Tune fusion weights on calibration split
• Sign package with Ed25519 private key
• Collect update and demo evidence logs
• Single source of truth for edge nodes
HTTPS · signed artifact manifest · Ed25519 verified
⬡ EDGE DEVICE / PEP NODE — offline-capable inference · verified artifact activation · runtime trust control
• Writes explicit evidence lines to log
• Reload KB and policy from sync state
• Log proof: Reloaded KB and policy
• Model path kept stable for runtime safety
T_final(x) = policy_control( calibrated_fusion( M(x), R(x), H(x) ) )
• Record update checks, verification, reload, and trust traces
• Export JSON/CSV logs for thesis figures and reproducible evaluation
• Compare static policy vs calibrated policy; demonstrate post-reload behaviour change
• Measure package size, verification time, and reload latency
• Mitigates tampered / corrupted / broken updates; preserves offline edge decisioning
• Full runtime Wasm model hot-swap is explicitly out of scope (future work)
LTCA v1.2.0 separates the decision plane from the update plane: inference remains fully local, while adaptation is delivered through verified cloud artifacts.
Runtime activation is implemented for policy and retrieval knowledge, enabling controlled behavioural change without destabilising the Wasm inference path.
Calibration improves decision control by externalising fusion weights and thresholds into policy.json rather than hardcoding them inside the runner.
The implemented system should be claimed as a secure, reproducible, cloud-assisted edge trust control pipeline — not as online learning or unrestricted live model evolution.
AAU · MSc Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity · Supervisors: Dr. Reza Farahani · Prof. Dr. Martin Gebser · Universität Klagenfurt
